description: Each transaction's value is signed by its direction: credits ('PRIJEM') are positive and withdrawals ('VYDAJ') are negative. Transactions of any other type are excluded from the average.

b.request: For each account, average its transaction amounts with PRIJEM positive and VYDAJ negative, excluding all other types; compare that average with the average of those signed amounts across all accounts, and return the 10 accounts with the largest positive difference, showing account ID, account average, and unrounded difference in descending order
b.sql: WITH signed_trans AS (SELECT account_id, CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE -amount END AS signed_amount FROM trans WHERE type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ')), account_avg AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(signed_amount) AS account_average FROM signed_trans GROUP BY account_id), global_avg AS (SELECT AVG(signed_amount) AS overall_average FROM signed_trans) SELECT a.account_id, a.account_average, a.account_average - g.overall_average AS difference FROM account_avg AS a CROSS JOIN global_avg AS g WHERE a.account_average > g.overall_average ORDER BY difference DESC, a.account_id LIMIT 10;

c.request: Which accounts have an average transaction amount above the average across all accounts? Give the account id, its average, and how much it exceeds the overall average. Show the top 10 by that excess, biggest first, unrounded. Each transaction's value is signed by its direction: credits ('PRIJEM') are positive and withdrawals ('VYDAJ') are negative. Transactions of any other type are excluded from the average.
c.sql: WITH account_averages AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS average_transaction_amount FROM trans WHERE type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ') GROUP BY account_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(average_transaction_amount) AS overall_average FROM account_averages) SELECT a.account_id, a.average_transaction_amount, a.average_transaction_amount - o.overall_average AS excess FROM account_averages AS a CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE a.average_transaction_amount > o.overall_average ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: For each account (`trans.account_id`), compute the average transaction amount, treating credits ('PRIJEM') as positive and withdrawals ('VYDAJ') as negative and ignoring transactions of any other or missing type. Then take the mean of these per-account averages. List the accounts whose average is strictly above that mean, showing the account id, its average, and how far above the mean it is. Show the top 10 by that difference, largest first, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH account_averages AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS average_amount FROM trans WHERE type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ') GROUP BY account_id), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS mean_amount FROM account_averages) SELECT a.account_id, a.average_amount, a.average_amount - m.mean_amount AS difference_above_mean FROM account_averages AS a CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m WHERE a.average_amount > m.mean_amount ORDER BY difference_above_mean DESC, a.account_id LIMIT 10

d.request: Which accounts have an average signed transaction value above the average across all accounts? Treat credits (`PRIJEM`) as positive, withdrawals (`VYDAJ`) as negative, and exclude transactions of other types. Return each account ID, its average, and the amount by which it exceeds the overall average. Show the top 10 by excess, largest first, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH account_averages AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS avg_signed_value FROM trans WHERE type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ') GROUP BY account_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_signed_value) AS overall_average FROM account_averages) SELECT a.account_id, a.avg_signed_value, a.avg_signed_value - o.overall_average AS excess FROM account_averages AS a CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE a.avg_signed_value > o.overall_average ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;
